text:
matt: Quick check-in — proposing we "flatten" the service authz surface across org/project/service keys to simplify runtime checks. sketch below, want concerns + migration notes.

julia: Flatten how? do you mean one canonical token with a namespace claim instead of multiple key types?

matt: Yeah — canonical API key that carries (principal_id, role_ids[], tenant_id?, audience). Then a small adapter layer at the edge maps legacy project/org keys into that canonical shape.

kevin: I like the idea for runtime simplification. main worry: we lose guardrails that current per-project keys give us (e.g. billing isolation and rate limits tied to project IDs).

matt: Good call. plan is to keep billing and quota metadata orthogonal: token stays canonical but we keep a lightweight projection table mapping principal->billing_account and project affinity for quotas. runtime checks use token.claims + projection cache.

rachel: projection table = another datastore/cache to maintain. ops cost? what's TTL strategy?

matt: TTL = 30s for perf-sensitive routes, 10m for low-traffic. projection updates on key rotation events. aim for eventual consistency in migration window.

julia: How do we handle fine-grained RBAC? current model encodes per-project role bindings in the key itself which makes checks cheap. If we offload to projection, we add a lookup step for every authz decision.

kevin: Could do fast-path caching for tokens that are high QPS (prefix cache by token hash). Also evaluate embedding a compact RBAC bitmap in the canonical token for common roles — limited size.

matt: Proposal: two-tier runtime. 1) tokens with embedded role bitmap => no projection hit. 2) tokens without bitmap => projection cache hit. Migration will populate bitmaps for existing high-traffic keys.

tanvi: How about delegation & impersonation flows? We have service-to-service proxying where actor chain matters. A single canonical token should still carry actor_chain[] or at least a parent_actor_id.

matt: We'll include an optional actor_chain claim (capped length) and a lightweight actor-provenance header for long chains. For very long chains, fall back to provenance_id that references a persisted trace entry.

infra-bot: Note: any design touching token size affects JWT vs opaque decisions. Current limit for header-based tokens is ~8KB in our gateways.

matt: Thanks infra-bot. Keep canonical tokens <= 4KB target. Use opaque references for heavy metadata, with fast lookup paths.

rachel: Rotation: do we migrate existing API keys to canonical shape at rotation time? or mint canonical equivalents and leave originals until expiry?

matt: Strategy: on rotation/mint -> issue canonical token + keep legacy mapping until deprecation window. For read-only tokens (old ones) we support a compatibility adapter that translates legacy key -> canonical claims on first use, caching mapping.

julia: Migration risk: what if someone reuses an old key in a context that expects bitmap roles? adapter must synthesize safe default (least privilege) to avoid accidental escalation.

matt: Yes defaulting to least privilege is required. Adapter must not elevate privileges; it can add constraints. We'll block any synthesized admin role.

kevin: Audit and telemetry: we need to track when a request used adapter mapping vs native canonical token. Otherwise rollout blind spots.

matt: Agreed. add a header x-auth-source: canonical|adapter|projection-cache-miss. Also tag traces and logs accordingly.

tanvi: Another edge: third-party integrations that only accept project-scoped keys today. Migration plan needs an export path and clear deprecation timeline for external partners.

matt: We'll publish a migration guide and a 6-month deprecation with weekly telemetry checks. We should also provide a small shim service to mint project-scoped compatibility tokens for partners during transition.

rachel: Ops checklist request: 1) projection datastore support (+scaling), 2) gateway adapter rollout with throttling, 3) telemetry flags, 4) canary on non-critical routes.

matt: I'll draft a playbook. For canary: start with internal-only routes and an opt-in header x-auth-canonical=true so teams can opt-in early.

kevin: Concurrency/atomicity question: when a key rotates, how do we avoid a window where projection cache shows new mapping but gateway still validates old token? Add rotation grace window on verification?

matt: We'll use rotation tokens with issued_at and not-before semantics. Gateways accept tokens for grace window of 2 minutes post-rotation but projection service publishes a rotation event that invalidates cached old mappings.

julia: Security review: ensure adapter can't be used to escalate via crafted claims. We'll require signed adapters only (trusted edges) and HSM-signed canonical tokens.

matt: Noted. HSM sign for canonical, adapter must be an internal-only translation layer. Also add attestation logs for adapter operations.

rachel: Action items: matt to produce RFC with sequence diagrams + data model, kevin to prototype token bitmap format (<=256 bits), tanvi to draft delegation chain format, julia to own security review, infra to estimate projection datastore cost.

matt: Thanks all. I'll post the RFC draft here by EOD tomorrow. If anyone objects to the approach or has examples of systems where flattening caused surprises, please reply. :thumbsup:

kevin: :thumbsup:

julia: Looks good, will review RFC.

tanvi: I'll sketch delegation examples and paste in RFC.

rachel: Adding infra-estimate to next oncall agenda.

infra-bot: Scheduled reminder set: authz-flattening RFC review - in 24h.
